title: Josephson network as a~model for high-temperature superconductor and beyond: Macroscopic quantum coherence probed by microwave absorption
abstract: Since the seminal experiment by Stankowski et al. [Phys. Rev. B 36, 7126 (1987)] on YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-x}$, Magnetically-Modulated Microwave Absorption (MMMA) has become an important technique for detecting the superconducting transition in inhomogeneous ceramic compounds. The rise of microwave absorption below $T_c$ is accompanied by several low-field anomalies, usually attributed to the weak links between superconducting grains showing the Josephson effect, or to the dynamics of Abrikosov-Josephson vortices. In this article, we briefly review selected theoretical models rationalizing MMMA spectra for high-temperature superconductors, focusing on the $3$-dimensional array of Josephson junctions with random parameters including the resistivity, capacity and inductance of each junction, showing characteristic absorption anomalies observed in the experiment. The implications for recently studied microwave absorption in Josephson junction qubits are also discussed.
summary: This paper develops theoretical models to explain microwave absorption anomalies (MMMA) observed in high-temperature superconductors using a 3D Josephson network model. By simulating the coupled dynamics of these junctions, the authors show how discrete resonances evolve into continuous spectra as the system size increases. The results successfully predict characteristic minima that align with experimental findings and draw parallels to superconducting quantum circuits.
main_problem: The paper aims to theoretically model Magnetically-Modulated Microwave Absorption (MMMA) spectra observed in inhomogeneous high-temperature superconductors.
main_result: Increasing the size of the Josephson network causes discrete resonance peaks to fill out and smooth, while residual minima persist at specific magnetic flux values that match experimental observations.
method: The authors employ numerical simulations solving coupled nonlinear differential equations derived from superconducting loop dynamics, supplemented by elementary analytical approximations for small vibrations.
model_or_system: The system is a 3D Josephson network modeled as an array of coupled Josephson junctions with random parameters. The dynamics are governed by flux quantization and junction electrodynamics, analogous to modeling high-Tc superconductors or Josephson qubits.
key_observables: Microwave absorption power ($	ilde{P}$) as a function of external magnetic flux ($	ilde{\Phi}_{	ext{ext},z}$), exhibiting characteristic anomalies and minima.
important_parameters: System size ($N$), junction parameters (resistivity, capacitance, inductance), and the applied external magnetic field $	ilde{\Phi}_{	ext{ext}}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes zero net current flowing through the lattice for large systems; approximations are used for small vibrations around minimum potential energy points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate theoretical models comparing absorption from superconducting loops, single junctions, and 3D networks. Figure 4(a) shows power evolution with system size $N$, while Figure 5 relates the model to Josephson qubit energy levels.
paper_structure: The paper reviews established theories (flux quantization, vortex dynamics), develops a lattice approach for 3D arrays, performs numerical simulations showing size-dependent spectral filling, and concludes by drawing analogies between superconducting lattices and quantum circuits like qubits.
why_interesting: The detailed modeling of collective nonlinear oscillations in Josephson junctions provides a rich platform for studying macroscopic quantum coherence, phase transitions, and the interplay between disorder and coherent quantum behavior, relevant to open quantum systems.
